text:
maria: Quick sync on collector topology tradeoffs — thinking about a hybrid model where agents stay thin and gateways do most of the heavy lifting. Draft goals: keep user bandwidth/CPU low, push retention/tenant-tier policy to a central place, and make rollouts per-tenant without huge exporter duplication.

raj: +1 on hybrid. Curious what "thin" means for agent though. do we parse spans? sample? enrich?

maria: Minimal parsing only. Agent should do: local sampling (head-based), batching, prefix/KV cache for repeated trace prefixes, and immediate drop if obvious invalid. Everything else (enrichment, resource normalization, exporter fanout) in gateway.

devon: that helps cost on edge devices. But gateways will need state for tenant policies and exporter mappings. how do we avoid per-tenant memory explosion?

maria: two ideas: 1) shared canonicalizer + per-tenant policy refs (policy id) so gateway looks up rule sets on demand, 2) cold policies loaded lazily + cache eviction by LRU. I want to avoid spinning up per-tenant process unless heavy traffic.

ian: raises: retention enforcement at gateway is tricky for spans (we store in buffer for retry). If we accept retention drop decisions at gateway, we need a way to mark for downstream exporters so they don't try again. maybe an ack/marker flow.

raj: agree. also quotas — should be enforced at agent for fast feedback (client rate limiting) and again at gateway for global fairness. dual enforcement means we need consistent counters or leaky-bucket with tolerances.

sophia: UX question: how do we present this in Console? Customers ask "Are my spans being sampled at edge or centrally?" We should expose per-route breakdown: agent sampling rate, gateway enforced sampling, export success.

maria: Console metric plan: per-route token-level graphs, per-tenant sampling config (policy id), and an event log for policy changes with canary tags. For rollouts: canary by tenant or by tag (dev/staging/prod).

devon: For per-signal pipelines — my take: keep separate pipelines for traces/metrics/logs at both agent and gateway. Agent config example: 
```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
      http:
processors:
  batch:
  tail_sampling:
exporters:
  local_buffer:
  gateway_forward:
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch, tail_sampling]
      exporters: [gateway_forward]
    metrics:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [gateway_forward]
```
This keeps signals independent so customers can opt different retention/sampling per signal.

ian: love the config example. One operational note: gateway_forward needs backpressure handling. If gateway is full, agent should slow down or drop based on tenant priority.

raj: How about routing policies for exporter fanout? e.g., route trace X to vendor A, vendor B for golden tenants, else just vendor A. We need a compact policy language or rule DSL.

maria: propose policy model: matchers (attributes, tenant, service.name), actions (sample, enrich, route to exporter set, retention ttl), priority. store as small descriptors referenced by id. Gateway evaluates and expands exporter sets.

devon: Performance question — runtime evaluation cost. If rules are expressive, evaluation per-span could be expensive. Consider compile-to-trie for common attribute matches and vectorized evaluation per batch.

maria: yep. compile policies into decision trees and cache compiled artifacts per-tenant. Fallback to generic policy for infrequent tenants.

ops-bot: deploy: collector-gateway v2.4 rolled to canary tenants: 95% success, 10% CPU uplift on gate nodes.

raj: ops-bot status noted. Given CPU uplift, we should pilot with reduced enrichment for canary. maybe defer heavy normalization to async job.

sophia: console UX for rollouts: show canary list, tier, observed latency/cpu, error rates, and toggle to promote. Also show estimated cost delta for promotion.

maria: on retention TTLs — gateways should attach retention headers to exported payloads so long-term storage (internal or vendor) can honor it. That makes enforcement explicit.

ian: re: buffers and retry: implement per-tenant buffers with soft-limits. once buffer > threshold, mark low-tier tenants as "best-effort" and shed before high-tier ones. metrics exported to console for transparency.

devon: Edge-case: if agent has a strict offline window (phone app), we should allow local disk buffer rotation but mark items with agent-id and policy-version so gateway can resolve when they arrive.

maria: agreed. also need an idempotency key / dedupe hint to avoid duplicate ingestion after retries.

raj: next steps: prototype a gateway policy cache + small agent that only samples and forwards. I'll spin up a quick perf run with 1000 tenants and 10k TPS to measure policy lookup cost.

maria: thanks. can we keep this thread for notes? if you attach the perf run logs, drop them here. Also Sophia, let's sketch Console wireframes once Raj has numbers.

sophia: will do. I'll draft a compact policy UI that maps directly to policy ids so teams can reason about what was applied.

ian: I'll add instrumentation hooks for buffer pressure and per-tenant eviction events.

devon: adding a small PoC branch with the agent config and a compiled policy cache. PR later today.

maria: perfect. tagging follow-ups: @raj (perf), @sophia (console), @ian (buffers), @devon (agent). thanks all :rocket:
